title: "Instrumental Variables"
---

## Readings

* [Chapter 19 of *The Effect*](https://www.theeffectbook.net/ch-InstrumentalVariables.html)

* [Imbens, G.W. & Angrist, J.D. (1994). Identification and estimation of local average treatment effects. *Econometrica, 62*(2). 467-475.](/resources/Identification_and_Estimation_of_Local_Average_Treatment_Effects.pdf)

* [Getting started with estimatr](https://declaredesign.org/r/estimatr/articles/getting-started.html)

* [Complier average treatment effects](https://evalsp21.classes.andrewheiss.com/example/cace/) - This is a nice introduction to using instrumental variables to estimate Complier Average Causal Effects (CACE; also referred to as Local Average Treatment Effect). CACE is often used in RCTs when their is a lack of compliance to the randomization assignment.

* [Technical Methods Report: Estimation and Identification of the Complier Average Causal Effect Parameter in Education RCTs](https://ies.ed.gov/sites/default/files/migrated/nces_pubs/ncee/pdf/20094040.pdf)
